rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO REGULATE THE SALE, PURCHASE AND POSSESSION OF TOXIC AND HAZARDOUS SUBSTANCES, INCLUDING SODIUM CYANIDE PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Toxic and Hazardous Substances Control of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Toxic and Hazardous Substances Control of 2004.\" To preserve our aquamarine resources and ensure our food supply, the bill seeks to regulate the sale/purchase, possession, use, transport, storage, transfer and disposal of toxic substances by requiring a permit from the Philippine National Police and the Department of the Interior and Local Government.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT UPGRADING THE SALARY GRADE LEVEL OF THE SCHOOLS DISTRICT SUPERVISORS FROM SALARY GRADE NINETEEN TO SALARY GRADE TWENTY-FOUR
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to correct the inequity in the present compensation scheme whereby Schools District Supervisors receive lower salaries than their underlings, the School Heads or Principals. It proposes to upgrade the salaries of District Supervisors from salary grade 19 to grade 24.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING A NATIONAL PROGRAM FOR FILIPINO GIFTED CHILDREN AND SCIENCE-ORIENTED YOUTH, PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth Act
rows.abstract: \"Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth Act.\" The bill seeks to provide scholarships, grants and other forms of incentives to deserving science students and gifted children. It proposes the creation of the Center for the Gifted Children and Science-Oriented Youth which shall identify and place them in appropriate educational institutions and assist them in securing jobs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on EDUCATION AND WELFARE OF SPECIAL PERSONS since 2004-11-09

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT STREAMLINING AND STRENGTHENING THE PHILIPPINE DISASTER PREPAREDNESS AND PREVENTION CAPABILITY, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: The Philippines Disaster Preparedness and Prevention Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Philippines Disaster Preparedness and Prevention Act of 2004.\" For a faster and more effective response to natural and man-made disasters and emergencies, the bill seeks to streamline and strengthen the National Disaster Management Council. It provides a mechanism for the allocation, release and monitoring of the national calamity fund.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-03-01

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2006-03-01

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PROMOTE AND ENHANCE PUBLIC SAFETY BY PROHIBITING CRANK CALLS TO ALL EMERGENCY HOTLINES AND PROVIDING PENALTY THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Anti-Crank Calls Act
rows.abstract: \"Anti-Crank Calls Act.\" Intended to protect existing emergency hotlines from illegitimate calls, the bill imposes a fine of PhP5,000.00;  imprisonment of 6 months and severance of of the caller's telephone line and/or blockage of his mobile line for all crank, sex, and unnecessary calls and other forms of illegitimate calls. In case a crank caller uses a pay phone, the punishment shall be one year imprisonment.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on INFORMATION COMMUNICATIONS TECHNOLOGY since 2004-11-09

rows.author: C122
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE TEACHING OF ECOLOGY IN ALL ELEMENTARY AND SECONDARY LEVELS, WHETHER PUBLIC OR PRIVATE, ALL THROUGHOUT THE COUNTRY AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: To equip out citizenry on the ways to deal with environmental problems, the bill requires all elementary and secondary schools, private and public, to teach ecology.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: C122
rows.mother_status: REPUBLIC ACT (RA09341) enacted on 2005-12-21
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT 9161 OTHERWISE KNOWN AS AN ACT ESTABLISHING REFORMS IN THE REGULATION OF RENTALS OF CERTAIN RESIDENTIAL UNITS, PROVIDING THE MECHANISMS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The measure raises the ceiling of the rental rates of residential units in the National Capital Region and other highly urbanized cities to PhP9,000.00 per month and in other areas to PhP6,000.00 per month beginning January 1, 2005 for a period of three years ending on December 31, 2007. It also mandates lessors not to increase rentals by more than 10% to be computed on a cumulative basis.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03356

committee_action.remarks:
Please refer to Substitute Bill No. 3356 (CR No. 133)
RA No. 9341

rows.author: C122
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING EMPLOYERS TO INFORM THEIR EMPLOYEES OF THEIR RIGHTS TO SOCIAL WELFARE BENEFITS, COLLECTIVE BARGAINING AGREEMENTS OR COMPANY POLICIES UNDER EXISTING LAWS IN WRITING ON THE FIRST DAY OF THEIR EMPLOYMENT AND EVERY TIME A PARTICULAR CONTINGENCY OCCURS
rows.abstract: More often than not, employees fail to avail themselves of the benefits due them under the laws because of ignorance. The bill directs every employer to inform his employee, in writing on the first day of his employment and every time a compensable contingency occurs, of the benefits the latter may avail of. The employee should also be informed of the collective bargaining agreements, company policies and practices and employee contracts arising from the employer-employee relationship.
rows.status: Consolidated into HB00376

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-28

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D019
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING AN ELECTIVE OFFICIAL IPSO FACTO RESIGNED FROM HIS ELECTIVE OFFICE UPON THE FILING OF HIS CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY
rows.abstract: Section 67 of the Omnibus Election Code is deemed unfair in its treatment of candidates as it exempts candidates for the positions of President and Vice President from resigning from the public office they are currently holding. The bill seeks to do declare all elective officials running for any office other than one he is holding in a permanent capacity as ipso facto resigned from his office upon filing of the certificate of candidacy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D019
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-30, transmitted to on 2006-09-07 and received by the Senate on 2006-09-07
rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF HEALTH MAINTENANCE ORGANIZATIONS (HMOs), PROVIDING THEM INCENTIVES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Health Maintenance Organization Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Health Maintenance Organization Act of 2004.\" To make quality health care available through affordable health insurance policies, the bill grants HMOs incentives to encourage the private sector to participate in the government's program. It defines the regulatory framework for the operations of health maintenance organizations (HMOs). It delineates the fundamental rights of members and the health care providers.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05119

rows.author: D015
rows.title_full: AN ACT SEPARATING AND CONVERTING THE IFUGAO COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY-IFUGAO COLLEGE OF ARTS AND TRADE [ISCAF-ICAT] LOCATED IN THE MUNICIPALITY OF LAGAWE, IFUGAO PROVINCE INTO A TESDA SUPERVISED SCHOOL IN COORDINATION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT (DOLE)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D015

rows.title_full: AN ACT IMPOSING STIFFER PENALTIES TO PERSONS CAUGHT DRIVING A MOTOR VEHICLE WHILE UNDER THE INFLUENCE OF ALCOHOL/LIQUOR AND/OR PROHIBITED DRUGS
rows.title_short: Deadly Driver Reduction Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Deadly Driver Reduction Act of 2004.\" The bill imposes stiffer penalties for driving under the influence of liquor or prohibited drugs ranging from prision correccional in its minimum term and a fine of PhP20,000 to prision correccional in its maximum term and a fine of PhP80,000.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04893

rows.author: D085
rows.mother_status: Printed copies distributed to members on 2007-01-24
rows.title_full: AN ACT ACCORDING EQUAL RIGHTS TO WIVES AND HUSBANDS IN THE PHILIPPINES BY AMENDING ARTICLES 333, 334 AND 344 OF ACT NUMBERED THREE THOUSAND EIGHT-HUNDRED AND FIFTEEN, AS AMENDED, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE REVISED PENAL CODE
rows.abstract: Articles 333 and 334 of the Revised Penal Code define the felonies of adultery and concubinage, respectively, Under the law, a wife in an adultery case incurs a heavier penalty than a husband in a concubinage case. This bill seeks to amend Articles 333 and 334 of the Revised Penal Code to attune it to the Constitutional mandate of fundamental equality of women and men before the law.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05729

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT GRANTING MATERNITY LEAVE BENEFITS TO UNMARRIED PREGNANT WOMEN WHO ARE IN GOVERNMENT SERVICE
rows.abstract: Unmarried pregnant women in the private sector enjoy maternity benefits under RA1161. This bill seeks to extend the same benefits to unmarried pregnant women in the government service by granting them maternity leave benefits equivalent to 60 days for normal delivery and 78 days in case of caesarian delivery.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT TO CREATE A NATIONAL WOMEN'S MUSEUM, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: National Filipino Women's Museum Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"National Filipino Women's Museum Act of 2003.\" The National Filipino Women's Museum shall be established to enshrine and commemorate the heritage, heroism and martyrdom of Filipino women who played significant roles in the country's struggle for liberation, justice, peace and prosperity.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2005-05-10, transmitted to on 2005-05-11 and received by the Senate on 2005-05-17
rows.title_full: AN ACT DECLARING NOVEMBER TWENTY-FIVE OF EVERY YEAR AS NATIONAL CONSCIOUSNESS DAY FOR THE ELIMINATION OF VIOLENCE AGAINST WOMEN
rows.abstract: The proposed nationwide observance of the National Consciousness Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women in November 25 of every year aims to raise the public's awareness on the problem of violence and the elimination of all violence against women.
rows.status: Substituted by HB03783

rows.author: D085
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-08-07, transmitted to on 2006-08-14 and received by the Senate on 2006-08-14
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING TITLE FOUR OF BOOK FOUR OF THE LABOR CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES PROVIDING FOR WOMEN AND GENDER EDUCATION IN THE WORKPLACE
rows.abstract: The bill requires every employer to give their employees and workers free annual seminars on women's rights, welfare, development and gender equality, RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995) and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003) in the workplace. The seminars shall use participatory and non-education modules prescribed by the National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women and other women's organizations.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05012

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING ALL RETIRED AND ACTIVE MILITARY AND POLICE PERSONNEL, INCLUDING OFFICERS, FROM BEING APPOINTED IN A CONCURRENT OR ANY OTHER CAPACITY TO THE POSITIONS OF SECRETARY, UNDERSECRETARY, HEAD OR MEMBER OF GOVERNING BODIES OF GOVERNMENT-OWNED OR -CONTROLLED CORPORATIONS AND AGENCIES AND OTHER EQUIVALENT POSITIONS
rows.abstract: To uphold civilian supremacy as mandated in the Constitution, the bill seeks to disqualify all military and police personnel, including officers, from appointment to the positions of secretary, undersecretary and heads or members of government-owned or controlled corporations. The prohibition shall apply even after the military or police officer has been separated from service including retirement.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on CIVIL SERVICE AND PROFESSIONAL REGULATION since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT INTEGRATING EDUCATION ON WOMEN, GIRLS AND GENDER RIGHTS, EQUALITY AND WELFARE IN ALL LEVELS OF PUBLIC AND PRIVATE SCHOOLS
rows.title_short: Women, Girls and Gender Education Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Women, Girls and Gender Education Act of 2003.\" The bill requires all public and private educational institutions, including computer, technical and vocational schools, to integrate in their curriculum women's rights, welfare, development and gender equality, RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995) and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE RIGHT TO SECURITY OF TENURE, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF, AMENDING PERTINENT PORTIONS OF THE LABOR CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Strengthening the Right to Security of Tenure Act of 2001
rows.abstract: \"Strengthening the Right to Security of Tenure Act of 2001.\" To address the current practice of contractualization, the bill stipulates that an employee is deemed regular from the time he is engaged to perform activities by the employer whether or not such activities are necessary or desirable in the usual business or trade of the employer except where the employment is fixed for a specific project the completion of which has been determined at the time of hiring. The bill also provides for the repeal of Article 81 and declares probationary and casual employment as illegal.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LABOR AND EMPLOYMENT since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 26 OF EXECUTIVE ACT NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227
rows.abstract: The bill seeks to grant the right to remarry to a Filipino citizen whose spouse was a Filipino citizen at the time of marriage and who, thereafter, acquired a foreign citizenship at the time a divorce was obtained. The Filipino citizen who remarries under these circumstances shall not be prosecuted for bigamy.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on REVISION OF LAWS since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2006-05-29, transmitted to on 2006-05-31 and received by the Senate on 2006-05-31
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING ARTICLE 177 OF EXECUTIVE ACT NO. 209, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE FAMILY CODE, AS AMENDED BY EXECUTIVE ORDER NO. 227
rows.abstract: Article 177 of the Family Code provides that only children conceived and born out of wedlock of parents who, at the time of the conception of the former, were not disqualified by any impediment to marry each other may be legitimated. The bill seeks to amend the provision, as follows \"CHILDREN CONCEIVED AND BORN OUTSIDE OF WEDLOCK OF PARENTS MAY BE LEGITIMIZED.\"
rows.status: Substituted by HB04244

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE INCLUSION IN THE HISTORY BOOKS OF ELEMENTARY, SECONDARY, AND COLLEGIATE CURRICULA THE LIVES AND HEROISM OF FILIPINO COMFORT WOMEN DURING THE JAPANESE OCCUPATION AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: The measure proposes to inform and educate our children on the lives, sacrifices and heroism of Filipino comfort women during the Japanese occupation. Their inclusion in history books would give due recognition to the courageous struggles of these women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A SECURED AND SEPARATE PRISON CELL FOR FEMALE PRISONERS IN EVERY DISTRICT, CITY AND MUNICIPAL JAIL, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE SECTION 63 OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6975
rows.abstract: There have been a number of reports of rape and sexual harassment of female prisoners by male prisoners. The bill provides for a secured, clean, safe, sanitary and separate jail for female prisoners in every district, city and municipal.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-28

rows.author: D085
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING WOMEN'S AND GIRLS' HUMAN RIGHTS AWARENESS PROGRAMS IN MEDIA, PROVIDING INCENTIVES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Women's and Girls' Human Rights Awareness Program in Media Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Women's and Girl's Human Rights Awareness Program in Media Act of 2003.\" The bill requires that a minimum of 15% of the daily air time of radio and television broadcasting networks be allotted for women's and girls' human rights programs and shows. The programs shall include, among others, the lives of Filipino heroines, RA 7877 (Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995) and RA 9208 (Anti-Trafficking in Persons Act of 2003 and the UN Declaration on the Rights of Women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC INFORMATION since 2004-07-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROHIBITING DRAG RACING AND PRESCRIBING  PENALTIES FOR VIOLATION THEREOF
rows.abstract: The bill bans drag racing and provides a penalty of prision correccional in its maximum period if held for betting purposes.  It allows drag racing only in duly authorized race tracts where safeguards are taken for the protection of racers and racing aficionados.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2004-07-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT INCREASING THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS AND LIKEWISE INCREASING THE ALLOCATION FOR BARANGAYS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF 1991
rows.abstract: The bill proposes to increase the share of local government units in the internal revenue allotment (IRA) from 40% to 45% starting in FY 2007. The proposed  5% increase shall be allocated to barangays in addition to the 20% allocation provided under Section 285 of the Local Government Code.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2004-07-28

rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2005-12-14, transmitted to on 2005-12-22 and received by the Senate on 2005-12-22
rows.title_full: AN ACT REQUIRING THE ESTABLISHMENT OF PROVINCIAL, CITY, MUNICIPAL AND BARANGAY LIBRARIES AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.abstract: Libraries constitute the cheapest source of knowledge and information. The bill seeks the establishment of libraries in every local government unit (LGU). The funding for the establishment, operation and maintenance of libraries shall be taken from the 20% economic development fund of the LGU.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04552

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on DANGEROUS DRUGS since 2004-07-28

rows.title_full: AN ACT EXTENDING THE PERIOD OF VALIDITY ON THE PRIVILEGES FOR MULTIPLE ENTRY VISA AND REENTRY PERMIT OF FILIPINO VETERANS AND THEIR IMMEDIATE FAMILY MEMBERS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE ACT GRANTING PERMANENT RESIDENT STATUS, OTHER RIGHTS AND PRIVILEGES TO FILIPINO VETERANS OF WORLD WAR II WHO ACQUIRED AMERICAN CITIZENSHIP UNDER THE UNITED STATES IMMIGRANT ACT OF 1990 AND ANY OTHER PRIOR ACTS FOR THESE PURPOSES
rows.abstract: The bill proposes that the multiple entry visa and reentry permit granted to Filipino veterans who have acquired American citizenship and their immediate family members be extended until their application for permanent resident status in the Philippines has been approved. This will save  them time, money and effort in having their visa or permit renewed.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2004-07-28

rows.title_short: The P125.00 Daily Acroos-the-Board Wage Increase Act
rows.abstract: \"The P125.00 Daily Across-the-Board Wage Increase Act\".  To alleviate the living condition of the working class, the bill mandates all employers in the private sector, whether agriculture or non-agricultural, regardless of capitalization and number of employees, to pay their workers an across-the-board increase of P125.00 daily.

rows.title_short: The Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"The Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention Act of 2004.\" Youth offenders should be treated differently from adult offenders. The bill intends to provide a just and humane system of treating juvenile offenders through a comprehensive approach toward rehabilitating and reintegrating them into society. It increases the age of criminal responsibility from nine to twelve years old.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05065

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO FURTHER PROMOTE THE DEVELOPMENT, UTILIZATION AND COMMERCIALIZATION OF RENEWABLE ENERGY SOURCES AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Renewable Energy Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Renewable Energy Act of 2003.\" The country has immense indigenous energy resources that can be utilized to mitigate our dependence on imported fuel. These renewable energy resources include biomass, solar, wind, geothermal, hydro and ocean energy and other emerging energy sources. The bill aims to accelerate the exploitation, development and utilization of these renewable energy sources to enable the country to attain energy self-sufficiency, energy afforability and rural electrification.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05563

rows.title_full: AN ACT REGULATING THE EDUCATION AND LICENSURE OF PHYSICIANS AND THE PRACTICE OF MEDICINE IN THE PHILIPPINES, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 2382, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Revised Philippine Medical Act
rows.abstract: \"Revised Philippine Medical Act.\" The bill seeks to standardize, upgrade and regulate medical courses including internship training. It provides for the supervision, control and regulation of the practice of medicine, the examination for registration and licensure of physicians, the integration of the medical profession under one national organization and the promotion of a continuing professional education program.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04861

rows.title_full: AN ACT RENAMING THE BOY SCOUTS OF THE PHILIPPINES TO SCOUT PHILIPPINES, DEFINING ITS OBJECTIVES, POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, REPEALING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 111, AS AMENDED
rows.title_short: Scouts Philippines Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Scouts Philippines Act of 2004.\" To enhance the practice of scouting in the country, the bill proposes the inclusion of girls into the Boy Scouts of the Philippines (BSP) and rename the same to the Scouts  Philippines. It proposes to grant the organization tax exemptions and to name the President as the Chief Scout of the Scouts Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on  since 2004-08-02

rows.author: C013
rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING SECTION 286 OF REPUBLIC ACT 7160, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE LOCAL GOVERNMENT CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES, PROVIDING FOR THE AUTOMATIC APPROPRIATION AND RELEASE OF THE INTERNAL REVENUE ALLOTMENT OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract: Section 286 of the Local Government Code provides for the automatic release of the internal revenue allotments to local government units. However, the provision does not provide for the automatic appropriations of the same. The bill provides for the automatic appropriation and release of the same to prevent delays in releases.
rows.status: Approved by the Committee on 2006-05-24

rows.title_full: AN ACT STRENGTHENING THE POLITICAL PARTY SYSTEM AND PROVIDING FUNDS THEREFOR
rows.title_short: Political Party Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Political Party Act of 2004.\" The bill seeks to provide the institutional framework which shall govern the system of political parties in the country to make them more responsive to the needs of their members and of their constituencies. It provides definitive guidelines to reengineer and re-invent our current system of traditional politics and discourage political chameleons and butterflies.
rows.status: Substituted by HB05877

rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING THE COOPERATIVE CODE OF THE PHILIPPINES TO BE KNOWN AS THE \"PHILIPPINE COOPERATIVE CODE OF 2004\"
rows.title_short: Philippine Cooperative Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Cooperative Act of 2004.\" It has been noted that the growth and development of cooperatives have remained slow despite the enactment of the Cooperatives Code. The bill seeks to strengthen the Cooperatives Code of the Philippines to attract more groups to organize themselves into cooperatives.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04602

rows.title_short: Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines
rows.abstract: \"Real Estate Service Act of the Philippines.\" The measure aims to professionalize and upgrade the real estate practice in the country to make it globally competitive. It provides for the creation of the Professional Regulatory Board which shall be tasked to supervise and monitor all real estate transactions, stabilize the prices of land and construction materials and ensure the collection of the correct amount of taxes.

rows.abstract: \"Women's and Children Crisis Act.\" The bill seeks to institutionalize in every city and province at least one Women's and Children's Crisis Center to provide temporary shelter to women and children victims of violence, assist victims needing medical care, provide guidance counseling, secure legal assistance and provide training and placement.

rows.title_short: Cellular Mobile Telephone Number Portability Act of 2004
rows.abstract: \"Cellular Mobile Telephone Number Portability Act of 2004.\" Cellular mobile telephone number portability (CMTNP) is defined as the right of a consumer to retain his cellular phone number when changing to another service provider. The bill requires service providers to give consumers the option to port telephone numbers between service providers by implementing the CMTNP throughout the network of cellular phone service providers.

rows.title_full: AN ACT TO PREVENT AND CONTROL MARINE POLLUTION FROM SHIPS AND FIXED AND FLOATING DRILLING RIGS AND OTHER FLATFORMS, PROVIDE PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Ship Pollution Prevention Act of 1998
rows.abstract: \"Ship Pollution Prevention Act of 1998.\" The measure seeks to formulate a comprehensive marine environment protection program to prevent and control pollution from Philippine ships, all ships operating within our territorial seas and all fixed and floating drilling rigs and other flatforms. It also aims to implement the provisions of the MARPOL 73/78 which is the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR A COMPREHENSIVE HAZARDOUS AND RADIOACTIVE WASTES MANAGEMENT, PROVIDING PENALTIES FOR VIOLATIONS THEREOF AND FOR OTHE PURPOSES
rows.title_short: Philippine Hazardous and Radioactive Wastes Management Act of 2003
rows.abstract: \"Philippine Hazardous and Radioactive Wastes Management Act of 2003.\" The bill establishes a system of waste storage, transport, treatment and disposal. Sets the criteria for identifying hazardous radioactive waste which contain carcinogens, mutagens or teratogens at levels dangerous to human life. Prohibits the entry and transit of radioactice wastes into the country.
